references.text: Laws concerning the right of the firstborn and the protection of a wife's rights in marriage, especially when a man has multiple wives.
The Hebrew word שְׁאֵר (she'er) is used here to refer to close relatives and sexual relations, illuminating the meaning of 'marital rights' in Exodus 21:10.
Jacob's marriage to both Leah and Rachel illustrates the practice of having multiple wives and the obligations toward each of them.
Rachel's complaint about childlessness and Jacob's response highlight a husband's duties within marriage.
Paul teaches about marital duties between husband and wife, including the right of conjugal relations (עֹנָה), echoing Exodus 21:10.
An exhortation to husbands to live with their wives in understanding and to honor them, reflecting the principle of not neglecting a wife's rights.
Husbands are to love their wives as their own bodies, providing for their needs and care, paralleling the obligations regarding food, clothing, and conjugal rights in Exodus 21:10.
Complementary laws concerning a man's duties in polygamy (protecting the first wife) and privileges granted to newly married men.
